lines.text: particular which he had never forgotten. It was the sermon
preached on the occasion of a harvest festival and in a year
when, owing to very bad weather, the harvest had been a
failure. In the course of his sermon my father had said: "If
the farmers were to say in present circumstances— Why
should we give thanks, seeing that after all our labour we
have gathered in hardly anything?' then the answer must
be: 'Give thanks for the fact that you were able to work!' "
That is certainly a very simple thought, but the fact that
just this thought had remained so firmly in the old man's
memory shows how a quite simple thought can often strike
people with surprise and shed light on their situation.
"Give thanks that you were able to work!" How many a sick
person would count himself fortunate if only he could work!
And to-day above all it should be clear to us when we recall
that so many of our friends who have been torn from their
work would give much if only they were allowed to carry on
with their normal job at home. Which of us can really doubt
that the very fact of our being allowed to work is in itself a
proof of God's goodness to us? And seeing that we are
permitted to work, are we going to lament and complain
that there are other people who are better off than our-
selves? Often we do not realize how well off we in fact are!
I believe that to-day especially we need to take the lesson
of our parable to heart. To-day a new social order is taking
shape in our midst; and we are asked to be serious about it
so that all inequalities in our social life, all class warfare, may
disappear and a new community of the people based on
social equality and equality of opportunity may be success-
fully established. Has our parable anything to say in
opposition to this idea? Nothing at all! We have in fact
already suggested that our text is not concerned to impart
teaching about the social order. On the contrary it is quite
right that in our human communal life we should be careful
to achieve an order of society that is based on justice, and in
which there will be given to every man who is capable of
work and glad to work equal opportunities of prosperity and
